notes: Scope: administrative departments and administrative secretaries of the Delhi (NCT), Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh governments, as of 2026-09-25. Delhi department list and portfolio-to-minister mapping is sourced from the Rekha Gupta ministry Wikipedia page's current portfolio-allocation table (Feb 2025 order, still current per the existing st-dl minister positions), cross-checked against individual department websites under delhi.gov.in (e.g. gad.delhi.gov.in, finance.delhi.gov.in); administrative secretaries were taken from each department's own 'Who's Who'/'Directory of Officers' page where the page had current data (9 of 36 Delhi departments; the rest showed 'No Data Available' or the page's listed officer contradicted other current postings (e.g. Transport's who's-who still names Ashish Kundra, who this same research shows currently posted as Ladakh's Home/Finance Secretary and Advisor -- so Delhi Transport's secretary was omitted as stale rather than guessed). Delhi's 'Law & Justice' vs 'Legislative Affairs' portfolio split across two ministers for one notified department, and the merger of 'Art & Culture' + 'Language' into one department, are both flagged inline. J&K: jk.gov.in was unreachable from this session (connection refused on every attempt, including via an alternate DNS path); the department list instead comes from a 2024-12-17 Wayback Machine snapshot of the portal's own department directory (39 named departments, with 'Education Department' split into School Education / Higher Education and 'Youth Services and Sports' added to match the current ministers' portfolios from the existing states-dl-jk-la.json), for 40 total. No live or archived current (2025-26) administrative-secretary posting list was found for J&K, so all J&K secretary positions are omitted per instructions rather than guessed. Ladakh: sourced live from ladakh.gov.in/departments/ (31 departments) plus each department's own page. Ladakh has no elected Council of Ministers, so headPositionId for every Ladakh department points to the Lieutenant Governor (st-la-pos-lieutenant-governor) rather than a minister, and no chief-secretary 'oversees' relation was added since no st-la-pos-chief-secretary exists in the reference file. This session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted by sibling research segments before this segment started, so all research here relied on WebFetch/curl against official portals, the Wayback Machine and Wikipedia's MediaWiki API only.
